name: espresso mule
instructions:
First drink recipe in this cookbook. Two ingredients: ginger ale + a shot of espresso, combined carefully.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- ginger ale (I use a sugar-free sparkling water version — ginger/lime flavored sparkling water; see notes)
- 1 shot of espresso

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Fill a cup half-full with ginger ale.
2. Put the cup directly under the espresso spigot so the espresso streams into the ginger ale as it brews. This is inherently a slow-add — the temperature differential still causes foam, but slower than a straight pour would.
3. When it foams (it will), skim off the foam with a spoon and throw it away — the high-CO2 foam isn't tasty. Repeat as needed until only the settled drink remains.
4. Serve.

(ALTERNATIVE — IDEAL, PLAN-AHEAD VERSION: refrigerate the espresso first so it goes in cold — mixes with the cold ginger ale at the same temperature and doesn't foam. See notes.)
notes:
=== TEMPERATURE DIFFERENTIAL CAUSES FOAM ERUPTION — HANDLING IT ===

Hot espresso + cold carbonated ginger ale = massive foam eruption if combined at their default temperatures. The heat destabilizes the CO2 all at once.

IDEAL: mix them at the SAME TEMPERATURE. Refrigerate the espresso first so it's cold when it hits the cold ginger ale. This is the cleanest approach — no foam at all — but requires planning ahead.

WHAT I ACTUALLY DO (SKIM THE FOAM APPROACH): fill a cup half-full with ginger ale, put it directly under the espresso spigot so the espresso streams into the ginger ale as it brews (which is inherently a slow-add). It will foam anyway. When it does, take a spoon and skim off all the high-CO2 foam and throw it away — the foam isn't tasty. What's left after skimming is the actual drink. This is the practical approach when you don't have pre-refrigerated espresso.

=== I USE SUGAR-FREE SPARKLING WATER GINGER ALE (GINGER/LIME FLAVORED SPARKLING WATER) ===

My version uses a sugar-free sparkling water product — flavored ginger/lime sparkling water — rather than a traditional sugared ginger ale. Cleaner, less sweet, and the ginger + lime + espresso combination reads more like a proper adult mule than the syrupy result you'd get from Canada Dry / Schweppes. If you want the traditional sugared-ginger-ale version, that works too, but it'll read sweeter and closer to a soda-fountain drink than a mule.
